title: Teach the skill-lint pointer matcher to read a multi-heading parenthetical
action: Per T4, scripts/skill_lint.mjs:107 searches for the literal substring `("<heading>")` -- a parenthetical containing exactly one quoted heading. skills/bee-hive/SKILL.md:120 writes `("Silent Bookkeeping", "Progress ticks")`, a perfectly reachable pointer the matcher cannot see, so the check has been reporting a false missing-pointer for as long as that line has carried two headings. Two workers this session read the warning, recorded it as 'pre-existing advisory, unrelated' and moved on -- which is what a false positive in an advisory check buys you. FIX: match a quoted heading inside a parenthetical regardless of how many headings share it. Capture the before state by running the lint and recording the false finding; author no probe script. Do not change skill_lint's exit-0 behavior in this cell -- flipping it to blocking is deferred (it carries other unresolved advisories).

truths: node scripts/skill_lint.mjs no longer reports a missing 'Progress ticks' pointer for bee-hive
A genuinely absent pointer is still reported
A heading quoted outside any parenthetical is still not accepted as a pointer
key_links: the check's intent -- the rule is reachable from the body -- is preserved, not widened to any mention
prohibitions: No change to skill_lint's exit code behavior
No weakening that would accept a bare mention with no parenthetical
No removal of any required-pointer entry

trace.outcome: skill_lint's pointer check now accepts a quoted heading anywhere inside a parenthetical (multi-heading and line-wrapped shapes included), clearing the false 'no pointer to Progress ticks' finding; a heading quoted outside every parenthetical is still not a pointer and exit-0 behavior is unchanged.
